supersedes: The scratch-model proposal in historical JOINT_TRAINING_DIRECTION.json; use pretrained Qwen as requested by the user.
objective: Test whether task-driven joint adaptation of gates and experts forms useful expert functions and improves quality-cost-stability tradeoffs.

models.revision_policy: Resolve and freeze a commit revision and SHA-256 inventory before any run; freeze tokenizer, special tokens and configuration too.

matrix.prior_quantum_comparison: Second frozen matrix: author-code expectation-readout reproduction and paper Born-readout variant from NOVELTY_REVIEW; document exact source revision/license and adaptation. Do not label local gate_arch=quantum as a faithful reproduction.

architecture.patched_layers: last_quarter, resolve and record explicit layer indices separately for each Qwen size
architecture.expert_initialization: One common conversion of pretrained dense weights per seed, reused byte-identically across gates. Inspect existing approximation/SVD utilities; record reconstruction error. Expert tensors must remain distinct within the model.
architecture.gate_initialization: Shared encoder tensors for compatible shapes; deterministic method-specific heads; record initial entropy, load and task loss. No trained MLP-router imitation warmstart.
architecture.trainable_scope: All MoTE experts, routers and conversion residual/tail parameters in selected layers; other pretrained weights fixed. Dense adaptation control updates corresponding original FFNs in the same layers.
architecture.dispatch_gradient: Use one explicitly documented hard-top-k and backward rule for every method. Test selected and unselected gradients; do not change STE semantics across methods.
architecture.parameter_matching: Report actual gate, expert, residual, total and trainable counts. CZ/product share shape and budget; include classical rank/width matching if differences materially affect conclusions.

task_training.primary_loss: Token-weighted next-token cross entropy on observed training text
task_training.optimizer: AdamW; FP32 optimizer states; no quantized optimizer in initial comparison
task_training.schedule: 5 percent linear warmup then cosine; progress measured in supervised tokens
task_training.token_accounting: Count shifted nonignored targets, not padded input length. Use fixed packed target windows and exact token-normalized gradient accumulation; DDP normalization must match single-device global updates.
task_training.formal_budget_policy: This is a bounded continued-training first round, not pretraining. Measure pilot throughput/cost and record a common budget decision before formal runs; any change creates a new config hash applied to the entire comparison.
task_training.precision: BF16 backbone/experts on capable GPUs; FP32 router computations and top-k outside autocast for every method. V100 FP16+GradScaler is a separate cohort. Disable TF32 for the primary comparison.
task_training.microbatch_policy: Tune only for hardware feasibility using the same pilot windows; retain global target-token budget/order. Record each change.

data_release.proposal: A bounded English continued-pretraining subset from HuggingFaceFW/fineweb sample-10BT, with resolved dataset revision, license and retained document IDs. All methods use the identical tokenized release. Alternative locally available corpus requires an explicit common revision before training.
data_release.split: Hash original document identity into train/internal_dev/reserved_test before tokenization/packing; audit duplicate or overlapping documents and keep document boundaries explicit.
data_release.sampling: Publish deterministic per-seed sample/order manifests. Share release across 0.6B/1.7B only after verifying tokenizer identity; otherwise publish separate tokenized releases over identical source documents.
data_release.selection: All architecture and hyperparameter decisions use internal_dev. Evaluate reserved_test only after the matrix, checkpoints and analysis choices are locked; report all methods/seeds.

evaluation.primary_checkpoint: Fixed final token budget for equal-token comparison; best internal_dev checkpoint is separately labeled secondary analysis.
evaluation.mechanism_protocol: Use fixed internal-dev windows and fixed perturbations; preserve actual sample IDs. Separate state QFI, sparse-weight Jacobian and downstream model risk. Match expert functions, not arbitrary expert IDs across independent runs.
evaluation.precision_probes: Distinguish input FP16/BF16 roundtrip, native autocast forward, and batch-shape changes. Compare each to its own FP32 reference. Label unsupported native precision on V100.
evaluation.timing: Serial isolated-device measurements with warmup and synchronization; include actual sparse dispatch, backbone and tokenization exclusions. Record GPU sharing. State KV-cache policy for generation.
evaluation.claims: Report different task-effective expert organizations as valid outcomes. Evaluate quantum structure gains against CZ/product and matched classical controls using the entire seed set.

release_acceptance: All four adapters integrated and output-contract/gradient/precision tests passed
Frozen model, tokenizer, data, code and resolved configuration hashes
Common expert initialization and per-seed sample order verified
Every method has finite nonzero router/expert gradients and measured parameter updates
No unwanted gate freeze, KD, margin, task mixing or default local dataset paths
Actual parameter counts, sparse execution and measured peak memory documented
Fresh-output refusal and owned-process lock checks
Full checkpoint includes model, optimizer, scheduler, scaler, RNG and data cursor; interrupted-vs-continuous replay tested
Short held-out-dev pilot completed for every method and dense control before choosing common formal budget
